title: Wittgenstein's Language Games
welcome_lead: Sit at Wittgenstein's table in as he overturns his own early work to find meaning in the use of words within forms of life.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on Wittgenstein's language games and their application to religion.
final_note: If meaning is use, then religious language is meaningful within the form of life it serves.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In the Tractatus (1921), Wittgenstein offered a picture theory of meaning: language pictures the facts of the world. Of what cannot be said, including the religious, we must be silent.

In the Philosophical Investigations (1953), he repudiates this and proposes that words derive meaning from their use within language games embedded in forms of life.

On the later view, 'God exists', 'I have sinned', or 'May God bless you' are not failed scientific claims but utterances at home in the language game of worship, confession, and blessing.

To learn their meaning is to be drawn into the form of life in which they function.

D.Z. Phillips' The Concept of Prayer (1965) applies Wittgenstein's later thought to religion. Petitionary prayer is not a primitive science of asking God to manipulate events but a way of bringing one's loves and fears into the presence of God.

Critics like Brian Davies worry that Phillips' approach drains religion of objective claims and reduces it to attitudes.

mcqs.q: What are James's four characteristics of mystical experience?
options: Religious experiences only happen during dreams.
Religious experiences are just hallucinations caused by stress.
Ineffability (beyond words), noetic quality (gives knowledge), transience (temporary), and passivity (feeling acted upon by something greater).
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Religious experiences only happen during dreams.
Jesus was half God and half human.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.

No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
The Buddha created the universe.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
